RE: LD 7 S, An Act to Update Funding for the Board of Environmental Protection Dear Sen. Tepler, Rep. Doudera, and Members of the ENR Committee:

My name is Ania Wright and I am Maine Audubon's Policy Advocate. Maine Audubon is a wildlife
conservation non-profit -- we fulfill our mission to "conserve Maine's wildlife and wildlife habitat" by
engaging people of all ages in nature through a science-based approach to education, conservation, and
advocacy. On behalf of Maine Audubon and our 30,000 members, supporters, and volunteers, thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support ofLD 75, An Act to Update Fundingfor the
Board ofEnvironmental Protection.
We are enthusiastic to support increased funding to support the Board of Environmental Protection
(BEP) as they continue to tackle some of the most difficult issues facing our wildlife and wildlife habitat. Whether it be the responsible siting of our critical renewable energy resources, or ensuring
adequate protection of our precious wetlands, the BEP covers a wide breadth of complex issues that require careful attention to detail and deep knowledge of our state's resources. As a citizen board, BEP members are tasked with an incredible amount of work, and we believe that members and DEP
supporting staff should be adequately supported.

In order to ensure timely and successful interpretation, administration, and enforcement of our critical environmental laws, it is vital that we adequately resource all work undertaken by the Board of Environmental Protection.

Sincerely,

Ania Wright Policy Advocate

Testimony of Rep. Dan Ankeles
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Environment and Natural Resources
Presenting LD 75, An Act To Update Funding for the Board of Environmental Protection

Senator Tepler, Representative Doudera, and fellow members of the Environment and Natural
Resources Coimnittee, thank you for the opportunity to testify today. I am Representative Dan
Ankeles, and I serve House District 100, a central slice of Brunswick that includes our downtown, Bowdoin College, the former naval airbase, Mere Point, Maquoit Bay and the Mere
Brook Watershed. It's an honor to bring you LD 75, An Act To Update Funding for the Board
of Environmental Protection, a measure submitted on behalf of the Department of Environmental Protection and the Board of Enviromnental Protection.
This bill increases from $325,000 annually to $450,000 annually the cap on the amount that may
be transferred to the Board of Environmental Protection Fund from the Maine Enviromnental Protection Fund, the Maine Ground and Surface Waters Clean~up and Response Fund, the Maine Hazardous Waste Fund and the Uncontrolled Sites Fund.
Many of you have seen legislation of this nature before. You have an entity like the Board whose needs have grown. Funding is available, but there is a fixed cap in statute that prevents the Board from making use of all the resources intended for it. The result is that the only way the Board can move forward is through the actions of this committee and eventually the full Legislature.
As of this writing, there is no fiscal analysis available online for me to refer to. But as you can
see from the bill summary, the Board is drawing its funding from Other Special Revenue accounts, or OSRs, and not the General Fund.
l'll leave it to the Board to explain why they feel they need this statutory transfer limit increased at this moment, but I think we would all have to be truly heartless monsters to say no to Bob
Duchesne. In all seriousness, I would make the case to my fellow committee members that we on
both sides of the aisle should value the Board of Enviromnental Protection because of the way it brings a broader range of perspectives to DEP's decision making process. This is especially
important in a policy area where regulations have a complex set of consequences and where the environment itself is also incredibly complex.

L.D. 75, An Act to Update Funding for the Board of Environmental Protection Page 2 of 2
The Department is authorized to transfer funding into the Board of Environmental Protection Fund from other Department funds proportional to each of those funds' contribution to the total special revenues received by the Department (38 M.R.S. �341G, sub-1). L.D. 75 would increase the amount of funding the Department can transfer into the account for the Board of Environmental Protection to cover costs for the two staff that serve the Board, meeting room rentals, transcriptions, and printing. All of these costs have increased since the statute was last amended in 2003. The Department has proposed increasing the current limit from $325,000 to $450,000 based on a review of expenditures over the last several years and projecting what adjusted annual limit would hopefully be sufficient for another twenty years. L.D. 75 will not increase fees.
Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony on L.D. 75. I am available to answer questions of the Committee, both now and at work session.
